# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:

  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.).   - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions

  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).

  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"

   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):

- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)

- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL

1	Both inputs read in full, plus the path/tier checks needed to make the manifest real. Four things I found change the plan's shape — flagged inline where they land.
2	
3	---
4	
5	# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan
6	
7	## 1. Goal statement
8	
9	Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns
14	
15	> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, 18 commits.**
16	> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
17	> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
18	> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.
19	
20	### Six branches, not one PR and not seven
21	
22	| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
23	|---|---|---|---|---|
24	| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
25	| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
26	| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
27	| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
28	| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
29	| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |
30	
31	Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.
32	
33	**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.
34	
35	### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away
36	
37	Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.
38	
39	### How much loop — scaled down deliberately
40	
41	| Branch | Loop | Why |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
44	| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
45	| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
46	| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
47	| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
48	| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |
49	
50	**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

180	#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)
181	
182	**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

186	**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

Reading the field with a fallback degrades to today's behaviour when absent and picks up the real value the day the hook ships. A shared constant would need reworking then.
323	
324	**Pass criteria.**
325	1. `maxOrderQuantity.test.ts` covers: `c_maxOrderQuantity` present → returns it; absent → returns 3; present but `0`, negative, or non-numeric → returns 3 (fallback, not a broken cap).
326	2. `cartItemMapper.test.ts` covers: full line item → all props; missing image → no crash and an `alt` still present; colour and size → **one** combined string in the documented order; quantity and `stepQuantity` passed through.
327	3. `grep -rn "useCurrentBasket\|useProduct\|commerce-sdk-react" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart* overrides/app/components/product-item overrides/app/components/item-variant` returns **nothing**.
328	4. No `const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3` typed anywhere new (no-magic-numbers), and `product-detail/index.tsx` is **not** modified — that is Squad B's file and refactoring upward is Hard Rule #5.
329	
330	#### Step 3.5 — Wire `ZimmQuantityStepper` + `maxOrderQuantity` into `product-item` (inserted 2026-09-18)
331	
332	**Why this step exists.** Not in the original plan. Found during the SFCC-795 accessibility sweep (originally step 3.5, now 3.6): `product-item/index.tsx` still renders base `ProductQuantityPicker` (unstyled base `QuantityPicker`) — `ZimmQuantityStepper` (step 3.1, commit `286deb09`) has zero production usage anywhere, and no later step in this plan ever wires it in. Confirmed by grepping the entire plan text before adding this step. Same root cause, same discovery: `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4, commit `f2612b92`) is not plumbed into the real stepper either — no `max` is ever passed to the real, currently-rendered component, so there is no live cap enforcement anywhere today. Marcel's call (2026-09-18): plan both wirings in now rather than leave them standalone indefinitely.
333	
334	**Changes.** In `product-item/index.tsx`, replace the `ProductQuantityPicker` branch (the `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity` is a separate, static display for free/bonus items and is out of this step's scope) with `ZimmQuantityStepper`. `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component (`quantity`/`min`/`max`/`isUnavailable`/`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`) — a different contract than `ProductQuantityPicker`'s `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split, so this is real integration, not a prop rename. Keep `product-item`'s own existing `quantity`/`setQuantity` local state; wire `onDecrement`/`onIncrement` to call the same `onItemQuantityChange`-then-conditionally-`setQuantity` flow the old `handleQuantityChange` used, adapted to the new callback shape (each receives the already-computed next value directly, unlike the old picker's raw string/number input-change event).
335	
336	`min={1}` — resolves the audit's own found discrepancy directly in the new stepper's favour: the old, real component floored at 0 (never actually speced or tested against ACs); `ZimmQuantityStepper` was built and tested against a floor of 1 since step 3.1 (AC3, "quantity 1: `−` is disabled"). `max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}` — the first real caller of the step 3.4 util, `product` here being the same raw object `product-item` already receives (the util's own input type accepts a product-shaped object with an optional `c_maxOrderQuantity`, satisfied structurally).
337	
338	`isUnavailable` — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already established as out of this whole epic's scope). Leave unset/`false` for this step, same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle step 3.2 already established for `message`. Do not invent a detection heuristic.
339	
340	**Pass criteria.**
341	1. `product-item/index.test.tsx`: with `product.c_maxOrderQuantity` absent, the rendered stepper's effective max resolves to 3 (the util's own fallback) — assert via the real DOM (e.g. clicking `+` from quantity 3 does nothing further, or the increment control's `aria-disabled` state at that boundary), not by asserting the util was called with the right arguments alone.
342	2. With `c_maxOrderQuantity: 5` on the product, the stepper allows incrementing up to 5 and no further.
343	3. At quantity 1, decrement is disabled (matches `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own step-3.1 tested contract, resolves the audit's floor-of-0-vs-1 finding).
344	4. `BonusProductQuantity`'s own render branch and props are unchanged — diff `product-item/index.tsx` and confirm nothing in that branch moved.
345	5. `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own existing test suite (step 3.1) still passes unmodified — this step wires an existing, already-tested component, it does not change its own contract.
346	6. Storybook: `product-item/index.stories.tsx`'s existing stories all still render without throwing (the swapped-in stepper needs `min`/`max`/`onDecrement`/`onIncrement`, confirm every existing story still supplies enough for it to render, adding args where a story genuinely needs them).
347	
348	#### Step 3.6 — Accessibility sweep against 795's 11 a11y ACs (renumbered from 3.5, 2026-09-18 — step 3.5 above now owns the stepper-wiring gap this sweep originally found)
349	
350	**Changes.** Mostly verification — the 11 accessibility ACs are each checked off explicitly, now against the *real*, newly-wired stepper from step 3.5, not the orphaned `ZimmQuantityStepper` story in isolation. One real fix included: `ZimmInlineMessage` is not programmatically associated with its line item today (DOM adjacency only, no explicit ARIA link) — Marcel's call (2026-09-18): cheap, fix it now as part of going through this checklist. Give the rendered message element a real `id` and reference it via `aria-describedby` on the quantity control it's describing (the message is about the item's quantity/availability state, which is what the stepper controls) — exact mechanism left to the implementer, following whatever pattern other associated-error-text components in this codebase (form field + validation message, if any exist) already use, or a straightforward `aria-describedby` pairing if none do.
351	
352	**Pass criteria.** One checkable line per AC, enumerated in the PR body, each naming the file and the assertion that proves it. At minimum: every `IconButton` has `aria-label`; every `<img>` has `alt`; quantity changes announce via a live region (base `product-quantity-picker` already ships a `VisuallyHidden role="status"` — preserve it, do not delete it in the restyle; **known pre-existing defect, confirmed unmodified base SFCC behaviour, out of this step's own scope to fix**: the announcement reads the static `product.quantity` prop, not the live interactive value, so it never actually updates — flagged, not silently left undocumented); stepper controls reachable and operable by keyboard alone (now against the real `ZimmQuantityStepper`); focus-visible ring present and distinguishable on stepper, both action links (**`ZimmCartItemActions`/step 4.4 doesn't exist yet — unverifiable until then, not a failure of this step**), and the drawer close; the inline message is programmatically associated with its line item (**the one real fix this step makes — was a genuine gap, not just an audit false-negative**); target sizes ≥24px; no colour-only state conveyance. Storybook a11y check green on every story in B3.
353	
354	**Known, disclosed, NOT fixed in this step (Tier 1 / cross-cutting, needs UI-designer sign-off, not this build's authority to resolve):** `text.muted` (`grey[300]`, `#969696`) fails WCAG AA contrast against white at the sizes this build renders it (measured 2.95:1, needs 4.5:1) — confirmed via the real Storybook a11y test-runner, not assumed. This is not new to this step or this epic: `colour.ts`'s own existing comment already flags `grey[300]` as an unresolved Handover self-contradiction (`#969696` vs `#939393` — checked: the alternate value doesn't fix the contrast problem either, both are too light). The same token is already shipped in 10+ other components across the storefront (footer, product card, product price, size chip, button, subscribe modal, icons) — this may already be a live accessibility issue outside this epic entirely, not something this step introduced. Ship to the current spec value per this repo's own established precedent for exactly this situation (`colour.ts`'s own "shipping the current value, confirm with the UI designer" comment) — raise with the UI designer post-build, do not silently drop it and do not invent a replacement value unilaterally.
355	
356	---
357	
358	### B4 — SFCC-250 + 272
359	
360	#### Step 4.1 — The merge call (must come first)
361	
362	**Consequence first.** Today, passwordless OTP sign-in from the wishlist auth drawer does **not** merge baskets. SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket is **orphaned — the shopper's items are gone, not miscounted.** Until this is fixed, SFCC-250's AC5 has nothing to cap and SFCC-272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. It is step one of B4 by necessity, not by preference.
363	
364	**Mechanism.** Base `use-auth-modal.js` pairs its own passwordless flow with a `mergeBasket` call. `useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge across. The social-IDP route is fine (it redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges); create-account correctly skips (a new customer has no prior basket). Only `LoginPasswordlessUser` is affected. `grep -rn "mergeBasket" overrides/` is empty — no Zimmermann code merges anything.

# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, 18 commits.**
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, owners read directly from `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS`. Not from `.claude/registry/*.md`.

---

## 4. Steps

Mechanical gates referenced below, run on every step: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npm run lint` clean · `npm run test` green (this is what runs `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token + `Zimm*`-namespacing guards, `recipeParts.test.ts`'s parts-vs-reads guard, and `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision guard) · `npm run audit:tokens` reports no new finding in the touched paths.

Styling rules every step inherits: `textStyle` → `var(--zimm-*)` → recipe → `sx` → `.scss`. Never a bare Chakra key. Never a raw hex/px/rem/em in a component file. Responsive steps are explicit media queries off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation` — the pattern `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already uses; do **not** add a third `BP` alias alongside `footerShared.ts`'s and `headerShared.ts`'s. Never Chakra's array shorthand in a recipe.

**Figma space-token mapping:** resolve each `alias/space/NNNN` to the named `--zimm-scale-*` step with the same px value; only seven numeric aliases exist (`025`, `700`, `1100`, `1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`), so verify each against `foundation/spacing.ts` and `foundation/zimmTokens.ts` before typing it rather than inferring from the number. Per §11.10(9), **use the token value, never Figma's decimal** — `12.655` and `8.944` are post-scale render artefacts of `space/1200` (48px) and `space/1000` (40px).

**No hover-reveal surface exists in this bundle** — the cart item's action links are always visible in every Figma frame. If one appears during build, it is `:hover, :has(:focus-visible)`, never `:focus-within`.

---

### B0 — Step 0: `cart` e2e area

**Pass criteria.**

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

#### Step 1.2 — `ZimmCartDrawer` organism

**Changes.** New organism at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/`, wrapping `ZimmDrawer` with `size="xLarge"`. Props only — `isOpen`, `onClose`, `itemCount`, `finalFocusRef`, `children`, plus a `messages` slot and a `footer` slot (the footer slot is what hosts SFCC-275's button group until SFCC-816 lands). Recipe `ZimmCartDrawer` with parts for the messages band, the content container, and the two-column/one-column grid.

Header title: `"BAG • {count}"` via `ZimmDrawer`'s existing `title` prop (AC1). Empty: `"YOUR BAG IS EMPTY"` — **header text only**; the empty *body* is SFCC-277's and arrives in B4 as a slotted component.

The 52px messages band reserves its height while empty (designer annotation §11.3.1, "to prevent the cart changing position depending on errors") — `minHeight` on the `messagesBand` part. Resolve 52px to its `--zimm-scale-*` step; do not type `52px`.

Layout per §11.10's derived responsive rule: desktop ≥1440 two columns (items 360 / totals 430 / 140 gutter, 128 page gutter, header 84); tablet 834 single column, **fluid width with a 32px gutter — never the computed 659.2**; mobile full-width single column, 32px gutter. Header height: **whatever `ZimmDrawer` already implements** — §11.11(3) is explicit that its sizing was reconciled with the designer during SFCC-831/926 and the cart nodes disagree with each other (108 vs 68).

**Pass criteria.**
1. Story `Default` renders with `itemCount={3}` and the header reads exactly `BAG • 3`.
2. Story `Empty` renders and the header reads exactly `YOUR BAG IS EMPTY`; the messages band is still present in the DOM with a resolved `min-height` equal to the 52px token (assert in `zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts`, not by eyeballing the story).
3. `index.test.tsx` asserts: Escape calls `onClose`; backdrop click calls `onClose`; close button calls `onClose`; after close, focus is on the element passed as `finalFocusRef` (AC7).
4. `index.test.tsx` asserts scroll position is **restored**, not merely unlocked, on close (AC8 — the note flags this specifically as needing verification rather than assumption).
5. `zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts` asserts the two-column grid above the desktop breakpoint and single-column at and below tablet, each as an explicit media query, and that the tablet step carries a 32px gutter token with no `659.2` anywhere in the file.
6. `recipeParts.test.ts` passes — every part read off `useMultiStyleConfig` in `index.tsx` is declared in the recipe's `parts`.
7. Recipe key is `ZimmCartDrawer` (namespaced) and registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.
8. Story `title` is `'Layout/ZimmCartDrawer'` per `components.md`'s categorisation (global chrome/structural).
9. Storybook a11y check passes on both stories (it is gated in `preview.tsx` — do not disable it).

**Skill.** `/new-component` for the scaffold.

### B2 — SFCC-270, copy-first override

#### Step 2.1 — Copy-first, then STOP

**Changes.** Copy all eight base files verbatim to their mirrored paths, convert each to `.tsx`, update imports, add a `console.log('[overrides] <filename>')` marker to each.

Sources:
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/{index,bonus-product-quantity,product-quantity-picker}.jsx`
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/{index,item-image,item-name,item-attributes,item-price}.jsx`

Do **not** copy the base `.test.js`/`.test.jsx` or `data.mock.js` — we write our own.

**Pass criteria.**
1. All eight files exist at their mirrored `overrides/` paths with `.tsx` extensions. Zero `.jsx` under `overrides/`.
2. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
3. **Zero functional diff.** `git diff --no-index` between each base `.jsx` and its converted `.tsx`, ignoring type annotations, import-path rewrites and the marker line, shows no logic change. The defaults-then-spread order in `item-image`, `item-attributes` and `item-price` is untouched at this step. The `item-name` bug fix is **step 2.2**, not here.
4. `product-item/index.tsx`'s internal imports of `item-variant/*` are rewritten to **relative paths** (`'../item-variant/item-image'`), not the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path. This is the interception rule from `overrideStyling.md` — the base path builds and runs correctly in the app but silently renders the **unstyled base** in Storybook and Vitest, because `.storybook/main.js` aliases the package straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it. Get this wrong and every story and test in B3 will be exercising base SFCC, not our override, and look fine doing it.
5. `product-item/index.tsx`'s imports of modules it is **not** also overriding (`shared/ui`, `responsive`, `loading-spinner`, `quantity-picker`, `utils/utils`, `hooks`) stay on the base path. The `shared/ui` barrel trap applies — do not attempt to override individual `shared/ui/<Name>` members; 208 base files import the barrel.
6. **STOP.** Present the eight files to Marcel. Confirm in the running app that each marker logs — including from the wishlist page and a checkout summary, not just the cart — before any functional change. Then remove the markers.

**Skill.** `/override-component`, if it exists in `.claude/skills/`; otherwise the copy-first rule in AGENTS.md directly.

#### Step 2.2 — Restyle to Figma + the `item-name` fix

**Changes.** Co-located recipes `product-item/product-item.css.ts` (exporting `ZimmCartItem`) and `item-variant/item-variant.css.ts` (exporting `ZimmCartItemVariant`). Replace `layerStyle="cardBordered"` and the Chakra array-shorthand geometry (`width={['88px','136px']}`, `display={['none','block',...]}`) with recipe parts and explicit media queries.

Figma values (§11.2): root gap 28px desktop / 24px mobile, align `center` desktop / `start` mobile; image group 132×198 desktop `object-cover` / 67×100 mobile `object-contain`, aspect 288/432, bg `ivory[200]`, `mix-blend-multiply`; Item Details gap 12px desktop / 24px mobile; Item Info column desktop / row-space-between mobile. Product name **uppercase**, `textStyle="productNames"`. Price `textStyle="price"`. Colour + size as **one combined string** ("Lilac Sand, One size"), 200px wide, `text.secondary` — SFCC-270's separate colour AC and size AC are **two ACs describing one element**, so do not build two nodes.

The regular-weight 12px caption (Figma `Default/Caption`) has no textStyle — gate finding #13. Use `textStyle="caption"` and override `fontWeight` to regular **in the recipe**, annotated. Do not add a textStyle to `foundation/typography.ts`; that is Tier 1 from a cart ticket.

Two load-bearing requirements from the decision record:
- **Keep defaults-then-spread.** `<Box width={zimmDefault} {...props}>`, never the reverse. `order-summary` calls `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` and must keep winning.
- **Fix `item-name`.** Base is `<Link {...props} color="black.600">` — spread before the colour, so no caller can ever override it. Move the spread after. No base caller passes `color`, so nothing changes for them.

Make the stepper slot and the actions slot **optional** on the override's render path — the digital gift-card variant has neither (§11.2). Physical gift cards render as a standard 198 item.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `product-item/index.test.tsx` asserts, with the line item mocked: image renders with an `alt`; name renders uppercase; price renders; the combined colour+size string renders as **one** text node containing both values.
2. `item-variant/index.test.tsx` asserts a caller-passed `width` on `CartItemVariantImage` **wins** over the Zimmermann default, and the same for `mr`. This is the regression that breaks `order-summary` if the spread order flips.
3. A test asserts `CartItemVariantName` accepts and applies a caller-passed `color` — proving the base bug is fixed and provable, not asserted.
4. Rendering `product-item` with no stepper and no actions produces neither in the DOM and throws nothing (gift-card API requirement).
5. `recipeGuards.test.ts` passes: recipe keys are `ZimmCartItem` / `ZimmCartItemVariant` (`Zimm*`-namespaced, so they cannot deep-merge with a base recipe), and no bare Chakra token key appears on a registered scale.
6. `recipeParts.test.ts` passes for both recipes.
7. `npm run audit:tokens` reports no new raw hex/px/rem/em in `product-item/` or `item-variant/`.
8. `grep -n "\[" product-item/index.tsx` shows no Chakra responsive array shorthand remaining in geometry props.
9. Stories exist at `Commerce/ProductItem` with `Default`, `GiftCard` (no stepper/actions), and `MultipleItems` variants.
10. Mobile: at 402px viewport in the story, nothing truncated or hidden (AC9) — assert no `text-overflow: ellipsis` and no `display: none` on name, price, colour/size, stepper or actions.

---

### B3 — SFCC-795 + 271, states and stepper

#### Step 3.1 — `ZimmQuantityStepper` molecule

**Changes.** New molecule composing two `ZimmButton`s at `size="icon"` around a value display. Gap **8px (`xs`)** per §11.11(1) — design showed a 12px gap around a 12px glyph with no touch target; we apply the system's 24px `minW`/`minH` (ZimmButton `icon` already is `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`), which adds 6px invisible padding each side, so 8px yields 14px apparent. Annotate exactly that, citing WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 and the Figma node literally named `touchTarget` at 24.

Disabled glyphs use `OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4` from `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmCartItemShared.ts` — Figma ships separate greyed SVGs; we use opacity. One constant, one file, read by both the recipe and the tests.

**Pass criteria — every state named, because a state absent here is absent from the Tester's brief and the Scorer's gate:**
1. Quantity 1: `−` is `disabled`, carries `aria-disabled` or the native attribute, renders at 0.4 opacity; clicking it does nothing and quantity stays 1 (AC3).
2. Quantity > 1: both enabled; `−` decrements by exactly 1; `+` increments by exactly 1 (ACs 1, 2).
3. Quantity at max: `+` disabled and greyed, `−` still enabled (795 stepper group).
4. Fully OOS or unavailable: **both** disabled and greyed (795 stepper group).
5. **Hover, focus-visible and active** are inherited from `ZimmButton`'s `icon` variant, which already carries `_hover`/`_focusVisible`/`_active`/`_disabled`. Assert in the recipe test that the focus-visible ring's resolved value is **not identical to the default state** — an invisible focus state is a WCAG 2.4.7 failure and is the exact bug `zimmButton.css.ts` records having already shipped once. Figma supplies no hover/focus node for the stepper; inheritance is the resolution, annotated at the point of use. Do not invent a value.
6. Each button has an `aria-label` (`IconButton` renders no visible text — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`).
7. Resolved target size of each control is ≥24×24 CSS px, asserted from the recipe, not measured in a browser.
8. `index.stories.tsx` has a `play` covering increment, decrement, and the disabled-at-1 boundary.

#### Step 3.2 — `ZimmInlineMessage` atom + error/warning states

**Changes.** New atom, variant-driven: `error` (`status.error`) / `warning` (`text.muted`). It sits **between the stepper and the actions row**, full width, `textStyle="caption"` with weight overridden to regular per gate #13. In error states the Item Details gap widens 12 → 16px — that is a recipe state on `ZimmCartItem`, not a prop on the message.

**Presentation only.** OOS / partial OOS triggering is SFCC-282 and Unavailable is SFCC-796 — both Sprint 6, Hazel's. Build prop-driven with stories; do not wire detection logic.

Copy, verbatim from Figma: fully OOS **"This item is unavailable"**; partial OOS **"Quantity unavailable in this size"**; max quantity **"Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size"**.

Per gate #4, max-quantity renders as the **warning** variant (grey, `text.muted`), not error — the design and SFCC-250 AC4 agree; CAI-017's word "error" means user-facing feedback, not the severity tier. Annotate that reconciliation inline.

Per gate #9, **there is no low-stock variant** — CAI-030 forbids low-stock messaging at cart level. Do not add one.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Stories: `Error`, `Warning`, plus one per copy string above. Each renders the exact copy.
2. `error` resolves to `var(--zimm-color-status-error)`; `warning` to `var(--zimm-color-text-muted)`. Both asserted in the recipe test against the token var, not a hex.
3. The organism recipe test asserts Item Details gap is the 12px token by default and the 16px token in the error state.
4. Message renders in DOM order **between** stepper and actions.
5. No `#9c0000`, `#969696` or any hex literal in either file — `npm run audit:tokens` clean.
6. No low-stock variant exists in the component's variant union.

#### Step 3.3 — Promotional price + discount label

**Changes.** The was/now mechanism **already exists** in base `display-price` (`priceData` with `listPrice`/`currentPrice`/`isOnSale`, renders `ListPrice` struck, already multiplies by quantity so it is line-item aware). Only the **discount label** ("20% off applied") is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired when the promotions engine lands. It renders beneath the stepper.

`display-price` has **no override** and is a shared SFCC internal. Do not override it in this step; if Zimmermann styling is needed later it goes through the bridge pattern (faithful default export, styling in a recipe).

**Pass criteria.**
1. With `isOnSale` and a `listPrice`, the struck "Was" and the "Now" both render, and both scale with quantity.
2. With a `discountLabel` prop, the label renders beneath the stepper; without it, no empty node is emitted.
3. `git status` shows no new file under `overrides/app/components/display-price/`.

#### Step 3.4 — `cartItemMapper` + `maxOrderQuantity` util

**Changes.** `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartItemMapper.ts` converts an SDK basket `productItem` to the override's props — the `productListCardMapper.ts` precedent from PR #85. This is what keeps every component in B3 prop-driven with no data-fetching hook in a leaf. `useIntl` is permitted in leaves (Context-backed exception); nothing else is.

`overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts` reads **`c_maxOrderQuantity` off the SCAPI product response with a fallback of 3** — gate finding #1. Do **not** promote `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` out of `product-detail/index.tsx:123` into a shared constant: the TSD for SFCC-268 shows a real BM site preference surfaced as `c_maxOrderQuantity` via an `afterGET` hook, with resolution order product override (SFCC-703) → site preference → hardcoded 3. Reading the field with a fallback degrades to today's behaviour when absent and picks up the real value the day the hook ships. A shared constant would need reworking then.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `maxOrderQuantity.test.ts` covers: `c_maxOrderQuantity` present → returns it; absent → returns 3; present but `0`, negative, or non-numeric → returns 3 (fallback, not a broken cap).
2. `cartItemMapper.test.ts` covers: full line item → all props; missing image → no crash and an `alt` still present; colour and size → **one** combined string in the documented order; quantity and `stepQuantity` passed through.
3. `grep -rn "useCurrentBasket\|useProduct\|commerce-sdk-react" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart* overrides/app/components/product-item overrides/app/components/item-variant` returns **nothing**.
4. No `const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3` typed anywhere new (no-magic-numbers), and `product-detail/index.tsx` is **not** modified — that is Squad B's file and refactoring upward is Hard Rule #5.

#### Step 3.5 — Wire `ZimmQuantityStepper` + `maxOrderQuantity` into `product-item` (inserted 2026-09-18)

**Why this step exists.** Not in the original plan. Found during the SFCC-795 accessibility sweep (originally step 3.5, now 3.6): `product-item/index.tsx` still renders base `ProductQuantityPicker` (unstyled base `QuantityPicker`) — `ZimmQuantityStepper` (step 3.1, commit `286deb09`) has zero production usage anywhere, and no later step in this plan ever wires it in. Confirmed by grepping the entire plan text before adding this step. Same root cause, same discovery: `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4, commit `f2612b92`) is not plumbed into the real stepper either — no `max` is ever passed to the real, currently-rendered component, so there is no live cap enforcement anywhere today. Marcel's call (2026-09-18): plan both wirings in now rather than leave them standalone indefinitely.

**Changes.** In `product-item/index.tsx`, replace the `ProductQuantityPicker` branch (the `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity` is a separate, static display for free/bonus items and is out of this step's scope) with `ZimmQuantityStepper`. `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component (`quantity`/`min`/`max`/`isUnavailable`/`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`) — a different contract than `ProductQuantityPicker`'s `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split, so this is real integration, not a prop rename. Keep `product-item`'s own existing `quantity`/`setQuantity` local state; wire `onDecrement`/`onIncrement` to call the same `onItemQuantityChange`-then-conditionally-`setQuantity` flow the old `handleQuantityChange` used, adapted to the new callback shape (each receives the already-computed next value directly, unlike the old picker's raw string/number input-change event).

`min={1}` — resolves the audit's own found discrepancy directly in the new stepper's favour: the old, real component floored at 0 (never actually speced or tested against ACs); `ZimmQuantityStepper` was built and tested against a floor of 1 since step 3.1 (AC3, "quantity 1: `−` is disabled"). `max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}` — the first real caller of the step 3.4 util, `product` here being the same raw object `product-item` already receives (the util's own input type accepts a product-shaped object with an optional `c_maxOrderQuantity`, satisfied structurally).

`isUnavailable` — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already established as out of this whole epic's scope). Leave unset/`false` for this step, same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle step 3.2 already established for `message`. Do not invent a detection heuristic.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `product-item/index.test.tsx`: with `product.c_maxOrderQuantity` absent, the rendered stepper's effective max resolves to 3 (the util's own fallback) — assert via the real DOM (e.g. clicking `+` from quantity 3 does nothing further, or the increment control's `aria-disabled` state at that boundary), not by asserting the util was called with the right arguments alone.
2. With `c_maxOrderQuantity: 5` on the product, the stepper allows incrementing up to 5 and no further.
3. At quantity 1, decrement is disabled (matches `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own step-3.1 tested contract, resolves the audit's floor-of-0-vs-1 finding).
4. `BonusProductQuantity`'s own render branch and props are unchanged — diff `product-item/index.tsx` and confirm nothing in that branch moved.
5. `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own existing test suite (step 3.1) still passes unmodified — this step wires an existing, already-tested component, it does not change its own contract.
6. Storybook: `product-item/index.stories.tsx`'s existing stories all still render without throwing (the swapped-in stepper needs `min`/`max`/`onDecrement`/`onIncrement`, confirm every existing story still supplies enough for it to render, adding args where a story genuinely needs them).

#### Step 3.6 — Accessibility sweep against 795's 11 a11y ACs (renumbered from 3.5, 2026-09-18 — step 3.5 above now owns the stepper-wiring gap this sweep originally found)

**Changes.** Mostly verification — the 11 accessibility ACs are each checked off explicitly, now against the *real*, newly-wired stepper from step 3.5, not the orphaned `ZimmQuantityStepper` story in isolation. One real fix included: `ZimmInlineMessage` is not programmatically associated with its line item today (DOM adjacency only, no explicit ARIA link) — Marcel's call (2026-09-18): cheap, fix it now as part of going through this checklist. Give the rendered message element a real `id` and reference it via `aria-describedby` on the quantity control it's describing (the message is about the item's quantity/availability state, which is what the stepper controls) — exact mechanism left to the implementer, following whatever pattern other associated-error-text components in this codebase (form field + validation message, if any exist) already use, or a straightforward `aria-describedby` pairing if none do.

**Pass criteria.** One checkable line per AC, enumerated in the PR body, each naming the file and the assertion that proves it. At minimum: every `IconButton` has `aria-label`; every `<img>` has `alt`; quantity changes announce via a live region (base `product-quantity-picker` already ships a `VisuallyHidden role="status"` — preserve it, do not delete it in the restyle; **known pre-existing defect, confirmed unmodified base SFCC behaviour, out of this step's own scope to fix**: the announcement reads the static `product.quantity` prop, not the live interactive value, so it never actually updates — flagged, not silently left undocumented); stepper controls reachable and operable by keyboard alone (now against the real `ZimmQuantityStepper`); focus-visible ring present and distinguishable on stepper, both action links (**`ZimmCartItemActions`/step 4.4 doesn't exist yet — unverifiable until then, not a failure of this step**), and the drawer close; the inline message is programmatically associated with its line item (**the one real fix this step makes — was a genuine gap, not just an audit false-negative**); target sizes ≥24px; no colour-only state conveyance. Storybook a11y check green on every story in B3.

**Known, disclosed, NOT fixed in this step (Tier 1 / cross-cutting, needs UI-designer sign-off, not this build's authority to resolve):** `text.muted` (`grey[300]`, `#969696`) fails WCAG AA contrast against white at the sizes this build renders it (measured 2.95:1, needs 4.5:1) — confirmed via the real Storybook a11y test-runner, not assumed. This is not new to this step or this epic: `colour.ts`'s own existing comment already flags `grey[300]` as an unresolved Handover self-contradiction (`#969696` vs `#939393` — checked: the alternate value doesn't fix the contrast problem either, both are too light). The same token is already shipped in 10+ other components across the storefront (footer, product card, product price, size chip, button, subscribe modal, icons) — this may already be a live accessibility issue outside this epic entirely, not something this step introduced. Ship to the current spec value per this repo's own established precedent for exactly this situation (`colour.ts`'s own "shipping the current value, confirm with the UI designer" comment) — raise with the UI designer post-build, do not silently drop it and do not invent a replacement value unilaterally.

---

### B4 — SFCC-250 + 272

#### Step 4.1 — The merge call (must come first)

**Consequence first.** Today, passwordless OTP sign-in from the wishlist auth drawer does **not** merge baskets. SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket is **orphaned — the shopper's items are gone, not miscounted.** Until this is fixed, SFCC-250's AC5 has nothing to cap and SFCC-272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. It is step one of B4 by necessity, not by preference.

**Mechanism.** Base `use-auth-modal.js` pairs its own passwordless flow with a `mergeBasket` call. `useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge across. The social-IDP route is fine (it redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges); create-account correctly skips (a new customer has no prior basket). Only `LoginPasswordlessUser` is affected. `grep -rn "mergeBasket" overrides/` is empty — no Zimmermann code merges anything.

**Written 2026-09-17, end of the planning session. Read this first, then the two files below.**

Everything needed to build is already written down. **Do not re-derive it.** If something here
disagrees with your own reading of the cards or the design, this file and its two companions win —
they were produced with the live sources open and every claim checked.

|---|---|---|

scope. §10 closes the three content questions. §8 records corrections to the planner's own output.

```
current branch   feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch   (clean, carries open PR #112)
develop          71025f18  == origin/develop                     (fast-forwarded this session)
tsc --noEmit     exit 0, clean baseline
```

**First action:**
```bash
git checkout develop && git pull --ff-only && git checkout -b feature/SFCC-11_cart
```
Never branch from the current branch — it carries PR #112.

## The shape

**One branch, one PR, 18 commits.** Commit order and messages: `plan.md` §11.
Step boundaries ARE commit boundaries. One commit per step, never more.

**The one hard gate: commit 4.** Copy-first — eight files copied, converted, `tsc` clean, markers
added, then **STOP**. Nothing proceeds until Marcel has observed all eight markers firing from
**three surfaces**: the cart, the account wishlist page, and a checkout summary. A machine cannot
score this step.

**The one adversarial pass: commit 13.** Prove `useIsMutating()` by making it fail on purpose first.

a **regression check**, not a light pass: `product-view` is consumed by the PDP, the quick-view
modal and the bonus-product modal.

## Settled — do not reopen

- The drawer **replaces both** the OOTB `AddToCartModal` and the `/cart` page. Base files stay
  mounted, just uncalled. `/cart` goes vestigial.
- The trigger is **SFCC-315's own scope** ("triggered from any surface on the site").

  plan.md's own step 3.4 text (§4), found stale by zm-tester during commit 10 and corrected here
  per this same document's own authority rule two paragraphs below ("§3/§4 are unchanged and
  authoritative"): the bare `??` above lets `0`/negative through uncaught, which step 3.4's actual
  pass criteria explicitly forbid. What was built instead: `getMaxOrderQuantity()`
  (`overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`) validates for a finite, positive number and falls
  back to its own independent constant (3) — deliberately NOT shared with `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY`,

  receives the full unfiltered product payload.

  (`overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` **does not exist** — that was a bad path from a

`marcelannavarro` verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` **and** repo `admin`

511	## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)
512	
513	Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
514	by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
515	Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
516	mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
517	dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
518	each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.
519	
520	1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
521	   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
522	   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
523	   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
524	   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
525	   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
526	2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
527	   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
528	   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
529	   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
530	   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
531	   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
532	   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
533	   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
534	3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
535	   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
536	   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
537	   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
538	   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
539	4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
540	   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
541	   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
542	   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
543	5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
544	   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
545	   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
546	   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
547	6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
548	   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
549	   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
550	   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
551	7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
552	   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
553	   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
554	   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
555	   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
556	8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
557	   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
558	   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.

dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.

1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.

is `type(scope): SFCC-NNN description`.

**Two things this ordering buys:**

- **Commit 18 puts the trigger last.** Under §2 it had to ship with B1. Here nothing is reachable
  until everything is built, and the review reads as "here is the thing, here is where we plug it
  in." A genuine gain from the single-PR shape.
- **Commit 4 preserves the copy-first pause intact.** Copy-first was never about branching — it is
  about not bundling the override copy with functional change. Commit 4 stops and waits for
  Marcel to observe all eight markers from the cart, the account wishlist page and a checkout
  summary. Nothing proceeds until that is recorded.
